record.title: Denmark pandemic prohibition on entry without worthy purpose
record.endpoint_type: selective easing; announced policy and contemporaneous tourist traffic report
record.scope: National entry regime including German land border and Öresund fixed link
record.crossings: National inbound admission regime. German land implementation: Sæd, Kruså and Frøslev remained available; ten other road crossings sealed in both directions. Øresund fixed link was subject to national admission rules; route-specific refusal counts not established.
record.exceptions: Danish citizens; residents, cross-border workers and other worthy purposes; freight exempt from admission ban but subject to checks and crossing/routing restrictions; return-home transit allowed. Exceptions changed over time, including expanded German/Nordic family, holiday-home and job-interview access by May25.
record.enforcement: Official police implementation report states 131 persons refused among 2,960 checked on German road crossings and trains on March14. No independent observation of those refusals established. Reuters separately reports German tourist traffic on June15.
record.consequences: Not independently established in this pass
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status extrapolation to 21 October 2026
record.context: See scope and source notes; national restrictions are recorded once, not once per neighbouring country.
record.uncertainty: June15 is a selective tourism phase marker, not termination of all inbound restrictions, not the first easing, and not a uniform endpoint for Germany and Sweden. May25 worthy-purpose expansion preceded it. Reuters reports German tourist queues on June15 but not complete admission outcomes. Route, category and extension history remain incomplete; no continuous interval is justified.

historical.duration_note: Selective and changing policy phases; no uniform operational endpoint or continuous closed interval established

followup_reviews.Researcher: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root/resume_r32_r33; R40 original researcher, not a separate challenger or human verifier
followup_reviews.Separate challenger: GPT-6 Astra Pro /root, separate same-model context
followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the Danish worthy-purpose admission restriction. The initial notice and police refusal count establish both the legal measure and officially reported implementation on the German frontier. Retain inbound non-exempt foreign travellers, with citizens, residents, workers, freight and return transit distinguished. Three German roads remained usable and ten others were sealed both ways. Expanded May access and conditional June tourism do not erase continuing restrictions. Retain EU023-R1’s initial 14 March noon to 13 April inclusive schedule and 30 date-boundary difference. It remains an ordered window, not the final operational endpoint. Later German tourist movement is corroboration of partial easing rather than all-cohort reopening. Retain Health and biosecurity / Human disease control, explicitly linked to the Danish COVID response. No new motive is inferred from economic arguments for later easing. Police sources are primary announcements or operational self-reports; the prime-minister transcript supports changed exceptions. Reuters separately observes tourist traffic. A later host update does not change Reuters’ June 2020 event date. Retain null coordinates and unlocated phase text. German refusal totals are not assigned to Øresund; national admission scope does not imply that every route shared identical physical barriers.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge

Audit completion records the review, not universal factual confirmation.
